rationale: The selected proof is one induction wrapped around several independent analytic obligations, so it is split along those obligations. All six children are self-contained Mathlib-only lemmas and are mutually independent (empty depends_on). Every use of the five sibling prerequisites stays in the parent's own assembly, because the Schauder estimate, difference_quotient_limit, holder_succ_iff_fderiv and holder_bilinear are not comparator-accepted and so cannot be reused as children; only holder_of_contDiffOn_succ is accepted, and only the parent needs it. How the children give the parent by the supplied proof. Base case m = 1, for each xb in U, direction e_k and R with closedBall(xb,4R) in U: (a) coeff_uniform_bounds with K = closedBall(xb,4R) gives Schauder hypotheses (H2) and (H3); (b) dq_uniform_bounds gives one M, independent of d, for (H4)-(H7) and the identity Dw_d = d^{-1}(Dv(.+de) - Dv); (c) dq_weak_equation gives Psi_d, with the same pointwise formula, and (H8); (H1) is the Legendre hypothesis; (d) the sibling Schauder estimate on B_{2R}(xb) bounds Dw_d on B_R(xb) uniformly in d, and the rewritten bounds are the hypotheses of the sibling difference-quotient limit, which gives D_k v in C^1 with alpha-Hoelder derivative on B_R(xb); (e) cover_holder_one makes this local C^{1,alpha} on U, and holder_succ_iff_fderiv ((C)=>(A), m = 1) gives IsLocallyHolderCkα 2. Inductive step m = m'+1 with m' >= 1: (a) holder_succ_iff_fderiv ((A)=>(B) and (A)=>(C)) gives Dv and v_s at level m'; (b) differentiated_system gives Psi_s and the weak equation for v_s; (c) on U, Psi_s(x)[P] = D_s(Phi(.)[P])(x) - sum_r pi_r(Dv(x)) D_s(a(.)[E_r][P])(x), a basis expansion of about 15 lines in the parent; (d) each product is handled by holder_bilinear with B = (mul R R).comp pi_r, and holder_loc_sub_sum assembles the regularity of x -> Psi_s(x)[P]; (e) holder_of_contDiffOn_succ lowers the coefficients to level m', the induction hypothesis gives v_s at level m'+1, and holder_succ_iff_fderiv ((C)=>(A)) concludes. Formal check of this composition: the six child types and the five sibling types were posed as axioms, and the exact frozen parent type was proved with no sorry (scratch file /tmp/lhr-decomp-ULIRRR/proj/Checks/Assembly.lean, about 220 lines; Nat.le_induction, base-case lemma, inductive-step lemma). #print axioms lists propext, Classical.choice, Quot.sound, all 6 children and all 5 siblings, so every child is needed. An independent adversarial review checked degenerate cases (n = 0, l = 0, K empty, e = 0, N = 0, j = 0, negative constants, global fderiv and rpow conventions). It found every child statement true, every English statement faithful to its Lean type, and every proof complete. Its three Lean-level notes are folded into the proofs: ContDiffAt.isSymmSndFDerivAt needs import Mathlib.Analysis.Calculus.FDeriv.Symmetric, the basis lemma is Module.Basis.sum_repr, and the lambda forms use fderiv_fun_sub and fderiv_fun_const_smul. subproblems.title: Local ball-wise C^{1,alpha} bounds give C^{1,alpha} on compact subsets (covering argument)
subproblems.statement: Let n be a natural number, E a real normed space, alpha > 0, U an open subset of R^n and F : R^n -> E. Assume every x in U has a radius R > 0 such that the open ball B_R(x) is contained in U, F is C^1 on B_R(x), and for some constant C, ||DF(y) - DF(z)|| <= C |y - z|^alpha for all y, z in B_R(x) (DF = fderiv). Then F is C^1 on U, and for every compact K contained in U there is C with ||D^1F(x) - D^1F(y)|| <= C |x - y|^alpha for all x, y in K, where D^1F = iteratedFDeriv R 1 F.
subproblems.lean_statement: ∀ (n : ℕ) (E : Type) [NormedAddCommGroup E] [NormedSpace ℝ E] (α : ℝ) (U : Set (Rn n)) (F : Rn n → E), 0 < α → IsOpen U → (∀ x ∈ U, ∃ R : ℝ, 0 < R ∧ ball x R ⊆ U ∧ ContDiffOn ℝ 1 F (ball x R) ∧ ∃ C : ℝ, ∀ y ∈ ball x R, ∀ z ∈ ball x R, ‖fderiv ℝ F y - fderiv ℝ F z‖ ≤ C * ‖y - z‖ ^ α) → ContDiffOn ℝ 1 F U ∧ ∀ K : Set (Rn n), IsCompact K → K ⊆ U → ∃ C : ℝ, ∀ x ∈ K, ∀ y ∈ K, ‖iteratedFDeriv ℝ 1 F x - iteratedFDeriv ℝ 1 F y‖ ≤ C * ‖x - y‖ ^ α
subproblems.natural_proof:
Source: step P3 (covering) of the parent proof, used in its step 6. B_r(x) denotes the open ball.
1. F is C^1 on U. For x in U let R_x be the radius from the hypothesis; u := B_{R_x}(x) is open, contains x, and U ∩ u = u, on which F is C^1. By locality of ContDiffOn (contDiffOn_of_locally_contDiffOn) F is C^1 on U.
2. DF is continuous on U. U is open and F is C^1 on U, so x ↦ fderiv R F x is continuous on U (ContDiffOn.continuousOn_fderiv_of_isOpen with 1 ≤ 1).
3. Fix a compact K ⊆ U. If K is empty every C works, so assume K ≠ ∅. By step 2 and compactness there is S ≥ 0 with ||DF(x)|| ≤ S for all x in K (IsCompact.exists_bound_of_continuousOn, then replace the bound by its maximum with 0).
4. Finite subcover. The open balls B_{R_x}(x), x in K, cover K. By compactness choose finitely many centres x_1, ..., x_N in K with K ⊆ B_1 ∪ ... ∪ B_N, B_i := B_{R_{x_i}}(x_i). Let C_i be the constant of the hypothesis for B_i and C_* := max(0, C_1, ..., C_N). Then ||DF(y) - DF(z)|| ≤ C_* |y - z|^alpha whenever y, z lie in a common B_i (as |y - z|^alpha ≥ 0).
5. Lebesgue number. Apply the Lebesgue number lemma (lebesgue_number_lemma_of_metric) to the compact K and the finite open cover (B_i): there is delta > 0 such that for every x in K there is i with B_delta(x) ⊆ B_i.
6. Near pairs. Let x, y in K with |x - y| < delta. Choose i with B_delta(x) ⊆ B_i. Then x and y both lie in B_delta(x) ⊆ B_i, so ||DF(x) - DF(y)|| ≤ C_* |x - y|^alpha.
7. Far pairs. Let x, y in K with |x - y| ≥ delta. Since alpha > 0, t ↦ t^alpha is monotone on [0, ∞), so |x - y|^alpha ≥ delta^alpha > 0, i.e. 1 ≤ delta^(-alpha) |x - y|^alpha. Hence ||DF(x) - DF(y)|| ≤ ||DF(x)|| + ||DF(y)|| ≤ 2S ≤ 2S delta^(-alpha) |x - y|^alpha.
8. With C := max(C_*, 2S delta^(-alpha)) steps 6 and 7 give ||DF(x) - DF(y)|| ≤ C |x - y|^alpha for all x, y in K.
9. Conversion to iteratedFDeriv. For every z, iteratedFDeriv R 1 F z is the image of fderiv R F z under the linear isometric equivalence (continuousMultilinearCurryFin1 R R^n E).symm (iteratedFDeriv_one_apply: iteratedFDeriv R 1 F z m = fderiv R F z (m 0); compare norm_iteratedFDeriv_one). By linearity, iteratedFDeriv R 1 F x - iteratedFDeriv R 1 F y is the image of fderiv R F x - fderiv R F y, and an isometry preserves norms, so ||D^1F(x) - D^1F(y)|| = ||DF(x) - DF(y)|| ≤ C |x - y|^alpha for x, y in K. Together with step 1 this proves the claim. QED
proof_key_steps: F is C^1 on U by locality; DF is continuous on U, hence bounded by S on K
finite subcover of K by hypothesis balls; C_* = max of their Hoelder constants
Lebesgue number delta: pairs closer than delta lie in one ball
pairs at distance >= delta: 2S <= 2S delta^(-alpha)|x-y|^alpha
||D^1F(x) - D^1F(y)|| = ||DF(x) - DF(y)|| via the curryFin1 isometry

subproblems.title: Uniform bound and uniform alpha-Hoelder bound for a bilinear-form field with C^1 components on a compact convex set
subproblems.statement: Let n, l be natural numbers, 0 < alpha <= 1, U an open subset of R^n, K a compact convex subset of U, L := L(R^n, R^l) with the operator norm, and a : R^n -> (continuous bilinear forms on L) such that for all P, Q in L the scalar function x ↦ a(x)[P][Q] is C^1 on U. Then there is M with |a(x)[P][Q]| <= M ||P|| ||Q|| and |a(x)[P][Q] - a(y)[P][Q]| <= M |x - y|^alpha ||P|| ||Q|| for all x, y in K and all P, Q in L.
subproblems.lean_statement: ∀ (n ℓ : ℕ) (α : ℝ) (U K : Set (Rn n)) (a : Rn n → (Rn n →L[ℝ] Rn ℓ) →L[ℝ] (Rn n →L[ℝ] Rn ℓ) →L[ℝ] ℝ), 0 < α → α ≤ 1 → IsOpen U → IsCompact K → Convex ℝ K → K ⊆ U → (∀ P Q : Rn n →L[ℝ] Rn ℓ, ContDiffOn ℝ 1 (fun x => a x P Q) U) → ∃ M : ℝ, ∀ x ∈ K, ∀ y ∈ K, ∀ P Q : Rn n →L[ℝ] Rn ℓ, |a x P Q| ≤ M * ‖P‖ * ‖Q‖ ∧ |a x P Q - a y P Q| ≤ M * ‖x - y‖ ^ α * ‖P‖ * ‖Q‖
subproblems.natural_proof:
Source: the bounds (H2), (H3) of step 4 of the parent proof, obtained there from P1 (components on a basis) and step 1 (Lipschitz, hence alpha-Hoelder, on the convex compact K0); here K is any compact convex subset of U.
Lean note: L := Rn n →L[ℝ] Rn ℓ has FiniteDimensional, and the linear-form type L →L[ℝ] ℝ has AddCommGroup/NormedSpace instances at the default maxSynthPendingDepth (checked at the pin). A basis is b := Module.finBasis ℝ L (index Fin (Module.finrank ℝ L)), coordinates π_r := LinearMap.toContinuousLinearMap (b.coord r) with π_r P = b.repr P r, and P = Σ_r b.repr P r • b r (Module.Basis.sum_repr, i.e. b.sum_repr P). No algebraic structure on the bilinear-form type L →L[ℝ] L →L[ℝ] ℝ is needed: only the scalars a x P Q are manipulated (if such structure is ever wanted, use set_option maxSynthPendingDepth 3).
1. Basis. L is finite-dimensional. Fix a basis E_1, ..., E_N of L and its coordinate functionals pi_r (linear, hence continuous on the finite-dimensional L), so that P = Σ_r pi_r(P) E_r. Let c := max(1, ||pi_1||, ..., ||pi_N||); then |pi_r(P)| ≤ c ||P||.
2. Expansion. For x in R^n put a_rt(x) := a(x)[E_r][E_t]. By bilinearity of a(x), a(x)[P][Q] = Σ_{r,t} pi_r(P) pi_t(Q) a_rt(x) for all P, Q.
3. If K is empty the claim is trivial; assume K ≠ ∅. Each a_rt is C^1 on the open set U, so a_rt and x ↦ D a_rt(x) (fderiv) are continuous on U (ContDiffOn.continuousOn, ContDiffOn.continuousOn_fderiv_of_isOpen). As K ⊆ U is compact and there are finitely many pairs (r, t), there are S ≥ 0 and S' ≥ 0 with |a_rt(x)| ≤ S and ||D a_rt(x)|| ≤ S' for all r, t and x in K.
4. Mean value. Every a_rt is differentiable at every point of K (K ⊆ U, U open), K is convex and ||D a_rt|| ≤ S' on K, so by the mean value inequality on convex sets (Convex.norm_image_sub_le_of_norm_fderiv_le) |a_rt(x) - a_rt(y)| ≤ S' |x - y| for x, y in K.
5. Lipschitz implies Hoelder. K is bounded: fix D ≥ 0 with |x - y| ≤ D for x, y in K. Let x, y in K. If x = y, then |x - y| = 0 = |x - y|^alpha (alpha > 0). If x ≠ y, then |x - y| = |x - y|^alpha |x - y|^(1 - alpha) (Real.rpow_add for the positive base |x - y|, with alpha + (1 - alpha) = 1) and |x - y|^(1 - alpha) ≤ D^(1 - alpha) because 1 - alpha ≥ 0 (Real.rpow_le_rpow). In both cases |x - y| ≤ D^(1 - alpha) |x - y|^alpha, hence |a_rt(x) - a_rt(y)| ≤ S' D^(1 - alpha) |x - y|^alpha.
6. Bounds for all P, Q. By steps 2 and 1, for x, y in K:
   |a(x)[P][Q]| ≤ Σ_{r,t} |pi_r(P)| |pi_t(Q)| |a_rt(x)| ≤ N^2 c^2 S ||P|| ||Q||, and
   |a(x)[P][Q] - a(y)[P][Q]| = |Σ_{r,t} pi_r(P) pi_t(Q) (a_rt(x) - a_rt(y))| ≤ N^2 c^2 S' D^(1 - alpha) |x - y|^alpha ||P|| ||Q||.
7. M := N^2 c^2 max(S, S' D^(1 - alpha)) satisfies both inequalities (all factors are nonnegative). QED
proof_key_steps: expand a(x)[P][Q] on a basis of L with coordinates bounded by c||P||
components and their derivatives are bounded on the compact K
mean value on the convex K: components Lipschitz, hence alpha-Hoelder since |x-y| <= D^(1-alpha)|x-y|^alpha
sum over the basis: M = N^2 c^2 max(S, S' D^(1-alpha))

subproblems.title: Difference quotients of a weak solution solve the translated weak system on B_{2R}
subproblems.statement: Let n, l be natural numbers, L := L(R^n, R^l), U an open subset of R^n, a : R^n -> (continuous bilinear forms on L), Phi : R^n -> (continuous linear forms on L), v : R^n -> R^l, xb, e in R^n and R, d real with R > 0, closedBall(xb, 4R) ⊆ U, |e| <= 1, d ≠ 0 and |d| < R. Assume x ↦ a(x)[P][Q] (all P, Q) and x ↦ Phi(x)[P] (all P) are continuous on U, v is C^1 on U, and the integral over U of a(x)[Dv(x)][Dzeta(x)] equals the integral over U of Phi(x)[Dzeta(x)] for every C^1 compactly supported zeta : R^n -> R^l with tsupport zeta ⊆ U. Then there is Psi : R^n -> (continuous linear forms on L) with Psi(x)[P] = d^{-1}(Phi(x + de)[P] - Phi(x)[P]) - d^{-1}(a(x + de)[Dv(x + de)][P] - a(x)[Dv(x + de)][P]) for all x, P, such that, with w(z) := d^{-1}(v(z + de) - v(z)) and B := B_{2R}(xb) (open ball), the integral over B of a(x)[Dw(x)][Dzeta(x)] equals the integral over B of Psi(x)[Dzeta(x)] for every C^1 compactly supported zeta with tsupport zeta ⊆ B.

subproblems.natural_proof:
Source: step 3 of the parent proof (equation for w_d). Integrals are Lebesgue integrals on R^n; B_r(x) is the open ball.
Lean note: L := Rn n →L[ℝ] Rn ℓ has FiniteDimensional, and the linear-form type L →L[ℝ] ℝ has AddCommGroup/NormedSpace instances at the default maxSynthPendingDepth (checked at the pin). A basis is b := Module.finBasis ℝ L (index Fin (Module.finrank ℝ L)), coordinates π_r := LinearMap.toContinuousLinearMap (b.coord r) with π_r P = b.repr P r, and P = Σ_r b.repr P r • b r (Module.Basis.sum_repr, i.e. b.sum_repr P). No algebraic structure on the bilinear-form type L →L[ℝ] L →L[ℝ] ℝ is needed: only the scalars a x P Q are manipulated (if such structure is ever wanted, use set_option maxSynthPendingDepth 3).
1. Definition of Psi. For x in R^n let Q_x := Dv(x + de) in L and Psi(x) := d^{-1} • (Phi(x + de) - Phi(x)) - d^{-1} • (a(x + de)[Q_x] - a(x)[Q_x]), an element of L* = L →L R (a(y)[Q] in L* is a(y) applied in its first slot). Evaluating at P (ContinuousLinearMap.sub_apply, smul_apply, smul_eq_mul) gives exactly the stated formula, for every x.
2. Geometry. Put B := B_{2R}(xb) and B3 := B_{3R}(xb). For x in B and t in [0, 1], |x + t d e - xb| < 2R + |d| |e| < 3R, so x + t d e lies in B3 ⊆ closedBall(xb, 4R) ⊆ U. In particular B ⊆ U, and x + de in U for x in B.
3. Continuity tools. Fix a basis E_1..E_N of L with continuous coordinate functionals pi_r. For all y, Q, P: a(y)[Q][P] = Σ_{r,t} pi_r(Q) pi_t(P) a(y)[E_r][E_t] and Phi(y)[P] = Σ_r pi_r(P) Phi(y)[E_r]. Hence if y0 is in U and y ↦ Q(y), y ↦ P(y) are continuous at y0, then y ↦ a(y)[Q(y)][P(y)] and y ↦ Phi(y)[P(y)] are continuous at y0 (the components are continuous within U at y0, and U is a neighbourhood of y0). Also Dv is continuous on U (v is C^1 on the open U; ContDiffOn.continuousOn_fderiv_of_isOpen).
4. Derivative of w. For x in B, v is differentiable at x and at x + de (both in the open U), so by fderiv_comp_add_right, fderiv_fun_sub and fderiv_fun_const_smul (the lambda-form versions of fderiv_sub, fderiv_const_smul), Dw(x) = d^{-1}(Dv(x + de) - Dv(x)).
5. Fix zeta, C^1 with compact support, with Kz := tsupport zeta ⊆ B; Kz is compact. Dzeta is continuous and Dzeta(x) = 0 for x outside Kz (tsupport_fderiv_subset). Consequently every integrand below, being linear in Dzeta(x), vanishes outside Kz.
6. Integrability. Define on R^n: f1(x) := a(x)[Dv(x)][Dzeta(x)], g1(x) := Phi(x)[Dzeta(x)], f2(x) := a(x)[Dv(x + de)][Dzeta(x)], f3(x) := a(x + de)[Dv(x + de)][Dzeta(x)], g3(x) := Phi(x + de)[Dzeta(x)]. Each is continuous at every point of Kz by step 3 (for x in Kz ⊆ B the points x and x + de lie in U by step 2, and the translation x ↦ x + de is continuous), and each vanishes on the open complement of Kz, hence is continuous there. So each is continuous on R^n with support in the compact Kz, hence integrable (Continuous.integrable_of_hasCompactSupport). As they vanish outside Kz ⊆ B ⊆ U, their integrals over B, over U and over R^n coincide (setIntegral_eq_integral_of_forall_compl_eq_zero, B and U being measurable).
7. Unshifted equation. zeta is admissible in the hypothesis (tsupport zeta ⊆ B ⊆ U), so by step 6, ∫ f1 = ∫ g1 (integrals over R^n).

Substituting y = x + de (translation invariance of Lebesgue measure, integral_add_right_eq_self) turns this into ∫ f3 = ∫ g3.

   by steps 7 and 8. This is the claimed identity. QED

Source: steps 1, 2 and 4 of the parent proof (bounds (H4)-(H7) for the difference-quotient system, uniform in d), including P1 and the scalar facts P2 for j = 1. B_r(x) is the open ball, D = fderiv.
Lean note: L := Rn n →L[ℝ] Rn ℓ has FiniteDimensional, and the linear-form type L →L[ℝ] ℝ has AddCommGroup/NormedSpace instances at the default maxSynthPendingDepth (checked at the pin). A basis is b := Module.finBasis ℝ L (index Fin (Module.finrank ℝ L)), coordinates π_r := LinearMap.toContinuousLinearMap (b.coord r) with π_r P = b.repr P r, and P = Σ_r b.repr P r • b r (Module.Basis.sum_repr, i.e. b.sum_repr P). No algebraic structure on the bilinear-form type L →L[ℝ] L →L[ℝ] ℝ is needed: only the scalars a x P Q are manipulated (if such structure is ever wanted, use set_option maxSynthPendingDepth 3).
1. Setup. K0 := closedBall(xb, 4R) is compact, convex and contained in U. Fix a basis E_1..E_N of L with continuous coordinate functionals pi_r, c := max(1, ||pi_r||), so |pi_r(P)| ≤ c ||P|| and P = Σ_r pi_r(P) E_r. Put a_rt(x) := a(x)[E_r][E_t] and Phi_r(x) := Phi(x)[E_r]. By (bi)linearity, for all x, Q, P: a(x)[Q][P] = Σ_{r,t} pi_r(Q) pi_t(P) a_rt(x) and Phi(x)[P] = Σ_r pi_r(P) Phi_r(x).
2. Hoelder constants on K0. For a function g that is C^1 on U and points x, y, ||iteratedFDeriv R 1 g x - iteratedFDeriv R 1 g y|| = ||Dg(x) - Dg(y)|| (iteratedFDeriv R 1 g z is the image of Dg(z) under the linear isometry (continuousMultilinearCurryFin1 R R^n _).symm; iteratedFDeriv_one_apply). Applying the hypotheses with the compact set K0 ⊆ U to the finitely many functions a_rt (P = E_r, Q = E_t) and Phi_r (P = E_r), and IsLocallyHolderCkα 1 alpha v U (v is C^1 on U and its first iterated derivative is alpha-Hoelder on K0), we get H ≥ 0 and H_v ≥ 0 with ||D a_rt(x) - D a_rt(y)|| ≤ H |x - y|^alpha, ||D Phi_r(x) - D Phi_r(y)|| ≤ H |x - y|^alpha and ||Dv(x) - Dv(y)|| ≤ H_v |x - y|^alpha for all x, y in K0 (take maxima with 0; the bounds remain valid since |x - y|^alpha ≥ 0).
3. Sup bounds on K0. D a_rt, D Phi_r and Dv are continuous on the open U (ContDiffOn.continuousOn_fderiv_of_isOpen), so there are S' ≥ 0 and S_v ≥ 0 with ||D a_rt|| ≤ S', ||D Phi_r|| ≤ S' (all r, t) and ||Dv|| ≤ S_v on K0.
4. Geometry. For x in B, |d| < R, |e| ≤ 1 and t in [0, 1] (or more generally |t| ≤ 1): |x + t d e - xb| < 2R + R, so x + t d e lies in B_{3R}(xb) ⊆ K0 ⊆ U. The same holds for every point x + s e with s in the closed interval between 0 and d.
5. Scalar difference-quotient lemma. Let g be one of the a_rt or Phi_r (C^1 on U, ||Dg|| ≤ S' and Dg alpha-Hoelder with H on K0) and let x, y in B. Then
   (a) |d^{-1}(g(x + de) - g(x))| ≤ S': by step 4 the segment from x to x + de lies in the convex K0, on which g is differentiable with ||Dg|| ≤ S', so the mean value inequality (Convex.norm_image_sub_le_of_norm_fderiv_le) gives |g(x + de) - g(x)| ≤ S' |d| |e| ≤ S' |d|.
   (b) |d^{-1}(g(x + de) - g(x)) - d^{-1}(g(y + de) - g(y))| ≤ H |x - y|^alpha: let I be the closed interval between 0 and d and h(s) := g(x + s e) - g(y + s e) for s in I. By step 4 the points x + s e, y + s e lie in K0 ⊆ U, so h is differentiable on I with h'(s) = Dg(x + s e) e - Dg(y + s e) e, and |h'(s)| ≤ ||Dg(x + s e) - Dg(y + s e)|| |e| ≤ H |x - y|^alpha because (x + s e) - (y + s e) = x - y. The mean value inequality on the convex interval I (Convex.norm_image_sub_le_of_norm_hasDerivWithin_le, or Convex.norm_image_sub_le_of_norm_deriv_le) gives |h(d) - h(0)| ≤ H |x - y|^alpha |d|. Since h(d) - h(0) = (g(x + de) - g(x)) - (g(y + de) - g(y)), dividing by |d| gives (b).
6. Claim (i). For x in B the segment from x to x + de lies in K0 (step 4), v is differentiable there and ||Dv|| ≤ S_v, so |v(x + de) - v(x)| ≤ S_v |d| |e| ≤ S_v |d| and |w_d(x)| = |d|^{-1} |v(x + de) - v(x)| ≤ S_v.
7. Claims (ii) and (iii). The translation z ↦ z + de maps B into U (step 4) and v is C^1 on U, so z ↦ v(z + de) is C^1 on B (ContDiffOn.comp with contDiff_id.add contDiff_const); v is C^1 on B ⊆ U; hence w_d = d^{-1} • (v(· + de) - v) is C^1 on B (ContDiffOn.sub, ContDiffOn.const_smul). For x in B, v is differentiable at x and at x + de (U open), so Dw_d(x) = d^{-1}(Dv(x + de) - Dv(x)) by fderiv_fun_const_smul, fderiv_fun_sub (lambda-form versions of fderiv_const_smul, fderiv_sub) and fderiv_comp_add_right.
8. Claim (iv). For x, y in B, by (iii) and step 2 (all four points x, y, x + de, y + de lie in K0, and (x + de) - (y + de) = x - y): ||Dw_d(x) - Dw_d(y)|| ≤ |d|^{-1}(||Dv(x + de) - Dv(y + de)|| + ||Dv(x) - Dv(y)||) ≤ 2 H_v |d|^{-1} |x - y|^alpha. So (iv) holds with the constant 2 H_v / |d|.
9. Claim (v). Write Q_x := Dv(x + de); by steps 3, 4, 2: ||Q_x|| ≤ S_v and ||Q_x - Q_y|| ≤ H_v |x - y|^alpha for x, y in B. Put q_r(x) := d^{-1}(Phi_r(x + de) - Phi_r(x)) and q_rt(x) := d^{-1}(a_rt(x + de) - a_rt(x)). By step 1, F_d(x, P) = Σ_r pi_r(P) q_r(x) - Σ_{r,t} pi_r(Q_x) pi_t(P) q_rt(x). Hence, using linearity of pi_r,
   F_d(x, P) - F_d(y, P) = Σ_r pi_r(P)(q_r(x) - q_r(y)) - Σ_{r,t} pi_t(P)[pi_r(Q_x)(q_rt(x) - q_rt(y)) + pi_r(Q_x - Q_y) q_rt(y)].
   By step 5: |q_r(x) - q_r(y)| ≤ H |x - y|^alpha, |q_rt(x) - q_rt(y)| ≤ H |x - y|^alpha and |q_rt(y)| ≤ S'. With |pi_t(P)| ≤ c ||P||, |pi_r(Q_x)| ≤ c S_v and |pi_r(Q_x - Q_y)| ≤ c H_v |x - y|^alpha:
   |F_d(x, P) - F_d(y, P)| ≤ [N c H + N^2 c^2 (S_v H + H_v S')] |x - y|^alpha ||P||.
10. Conclusion. M := max(S_v, N c H + N^2 c^2 (S_v H + H_v S')) does not depend on d; by steps 6 and 9 it satisfies (i) and (v) for every admissible d, and (ii)-(iv) hold for every such d by steps 7 and 8. QED

Source: step 8 of the parent proof (differentiated system, obtained by testing with difference quotients of the test function), for a general direction e. D = fderiv; integrals are Lebesgue integrals on R^n.
Lean note: L := Rn n →L[ℝ] Rn ℓ has FiniteDimensional, and the linear-form type L →L[ℝ] ℝ has AddCommGroup/NormedSpace instances at the default maxSynthPendingDepth (checked at the pin). A basis is b := Module.finBasis ℝ L (index Fin (Module.finrank ℝ L)), coordinates π_r := LinearMap.toContinuousLinearMap (b.coord r) with π_r P = b.repr P r, and P = Σ_r b.repr P r • b r (Module.Basis.sum_repr, i.e. b.sum_repr P). No algebraic structure on the bilinear-form type L →L[ℝ] L →L[ℝ] ℝ is needed: only the scalars a x P Q are manipulated (if such structure is ever wanted, use set_option maxSynthPendingDepth 3).
1. Basis and components. Fix a basis E_1..E_N of L with continuous coordinate functionals pi_r, c := max(1, ||pi_r||), so |pi_r(P)| ≤ c ||P||. Put a_rt(z) := a(z)[E_r][E_t] and Phi_r(z) := Phi(z)[E_r]; these are C^1 on U. For all z, Q, P: a(z)[Q][P] = Σ_{r,t} pi_r(Q) pi_t(P) a_rt(z) and Phi(z)[P] = Σ_r pi_r(P) Phi_r(z).
2. Definition of Psi and the pointwise formula. For x in U let k_r(x) := D Phi_r(x) e - Σ_t pi_t(Dv(x)) D a_tr(x) e and Psi(x) := Σ_r k_r(x) • pi_r in L* (a finite combination of continuous functionals); for x outside U let Psi(x) := 0. Let x in U and P, Q in L. The functions Phi_r, a_tr are differentiable at x (C^1 on the open U), so by step 1 and linearity of the derivative (fderiv_fun_sum, fderiv_const_mul): D(Phi(.)[P])(x) e = Σ_r pi_r(P) D Phi_r(x) e and D(a(.)[Q][P])(x) e = Σ_{t,r} pi_t(Q) pi_r(P) D a_tr(x) e. With Q := Dv(x) this gives Psi(x)[P] = Σ_r pi_r(P) k_r(x) = D(Phi(.)[P])(x) e - D(a(.)[Dv(x)][P])(x) e, the stated formula. Each k_r is continuous on U (Dv, D Phi_r, D a_tr are continuous on the open U).
3. Symmetry of the second derivative. v is C^2 on the open U, so for x in U, D(Dv)(x) exists, x ↦ D(Dv)(x) is continuous on U, and D^2 v(x) is symmetric (ContDiffAt.isSymmSndFDerivAt, as minSmoothness R 2 = 2; Lean note: this lemma lives in Mathlib.Analysis.Calculus.FDeriv.Symmetric, which the frozen Submission header does not import, so add `import Mathlib.Analysis.Calculus.FDeriv.Symmetric` to Submission.lean, as other branches of this run add Mathlib imports). With v_e(z) = Dv(z) e, for x in U and h in R^n: Dv_e(x) h = (D(Dv)(x) h) e (fderiv_clm_apply with the constant e) = (D(Dv)(x) e) h (symmetry). Hence Dv_e(x) = T(x) := D(Dv)(x) e in L for x in U; in particular Dv_e is continuous on U.
4. Compact thickening. Fix zeta, C^1 with compact support, Kz := tsupport zeta ⊆ U (compact). Choose delta > 0 with K1 := cthickening(delta, Kz) ⊆ U (IsCompact.exists_cthickening_subset_open); K1 is compact (IsCompact.cthickening). Put h0 := delta / (|e| + 1) > 0; then y + s e lies in K1 for y in Kz and |s| ≤ h0. (The argument below also covers e = 0.) Dzeta is continuous with Dzeta = 0 outside Kz (tsupport_fderiv_subset); let Z := sup ||Dzeta||.
5. The tested identity. Let 0 < |h| ≤ h0 and phi_h(x) := h^{-1}(zeta(x) - zeta(x - h e)). It is C^1 with compact support, tsupport phi_h ⊆ Kz ∪ (Kz + h e) ⊆ K1 ⊆ U, and Dphi_h(x) = h^{-1}(Dzeta(x) - Dzeta(x - h e)) (fderiv_comp_sub, fderiv_fun_sub, fderiv_fun_const_smul). As in the difference-quotient lemma, every integrand below is continuous on R^n with compact support contained in K1 ⊆ U (continuity at points of the support by the basis expansion of step 1 and continuity of Dv on U, vanishing on the open complement of the support), hence integrable, and integrals over U equal integrals over R^n. Testing the hypothesis with phi_h, splitting the integrals, and substituting x = y + h e in the terms containing Dzeta(x - h e) (translation invariance, integral_add_right_eq_self) gives
   h^{-1}(∫ a(y)[Dv(y)][Dzeta(y)] dy - ∫ a(y + h e)[Dv(y + h e)][Dzeta(y)] dy) = h^{-1}(∫ Phi(y)[Dzeta(y)] dy - ∫ Phi(y + h e)[Dzeta(y)] dy),
   that is ∫ G_h = 0 with G_h(y) := h^{-1}(a(y + h e)[Dv(y + h e)][Dzeta(y)] - a(y)[Dv(y)][Dzeta(y)]) - h^{-1}(Phi(y + h e)[Dzeta(y)] - Phi(y)[Dzeta(y)]). G_h vanishes outside Kz.
6. The limit integrand. Put G_0(y) := a(y)[Dv_e(y)][Dzeta(y)] - Psi(y)[Dzeta(y)] for y in U and G_0(y) := 0 otherwise; G_0 vanishes outside Kz, and by steps 2, 3 and 1 it is continuous on R^n with compact support (hence integrable). For y in Kz and P := Dzeta(y), adding and subtracting a(y + h e)[Dv(y)][P]:
   G_h(y) = a(y + h e)[h^{-1}(Dv(y + h e) - Dv(y))][P] + Σ_{r,t} pi_r(Dv(y)) pi_t(P) h^{-1}(a_rt(y + h e) - a_rt(y)) - Σ_r pi_r(P) h^{-1}(Phi_r(y + h e) - Phi_r(y)),
   G_0(y) = a(y)[T(y)][P] + Σ_{r,t} pi_r(Dv(y)) pi_t(P) D a_rt(y) e - Σ_r pi_r(P) D Phi_r(y) e   (by steps 2 and 3).
7. Uniform convergence on Kz. For g C^1 on U with values in a normed space (g = a_rt, Phi_r with values in R, or g = Dv with values in L, whose derivative D(Dv) is continuous on U), Dg is uniformly continuous on the compact K1 (IsCompact.uniformContinuousOn_of_continuous); let omega_g(rho) := sup{||Dg(z) - Dg(z')|| : z, z' in K1, |z - z'| ≤ rho}, so omega_g(rho) → 0 as rho → 0. For y in Kz and 0 < |h| ≤ h0, the mean value inequality applied to s ↦ g(y + s e) - s Dg(y) e on the interval between 0 and h (whose points y + s e lie in K1) gives ||h^{-1}(g(y + h e) - g(y)) - Dg(y) e|| ≤ |e| omega_g(|h| |e|). Likewise |a_rt(y + h e) - a_rt(y)| ≤ omega0_rt(|h| |e|), with omega0_rt the modulus of uniform continuity of a_rt on K1. On the compacts Kz, K1 the quantities |a_rt|, ||Dv||, ||T|| are bounded (continuity), and |pi_t(P)| ≤ c Z. Subtracting the two expressions of step 6 term by term, writing a(y + h e)[A][P] - a(y)[T(y)][P] = Σ_{r,t} pi_t(P)[pi_r(A - T(y)) a_rt(y + h e) + pi_r(T(y))(a_rt(y + h e) - a_rt(y))] with A := h^{-1}(Dv(y + h e) - Dv(y)), each difference is bounded by a constant (independent of y and h) times one of |e| omega_g(|h| |e|) or omega0_rt(|h| |e|). Hence sup_{y in Kz} |G_h(y) - G_0(y)| → 0 as h → 0.
8. Passage to the limit. Since G_h and G_0 vanish outside Kz and Kz has finite Lebesgue measure, |∫ G_h - ∫ G_0| ≤ vol(Kz) sup_{Kz} |G_h - G_0| → 0 as h → 0 (h ≠ 0). As ∫ G_h = 0 for all 0 < |h| ≤ h0 (step 5), ∫ G_0 = 0.
9. Conclusion. The integrands y ↦ a(y)[Dv_e(y)][Dzeta(y)] and y ↦ Psi(y)[Dzeta(y)] are continuous on R^n with compact support in Kz ⊆ U (steps 2, 3), so their integrals over U equal those over R^n, are finite, and their difference is ∫ G_0 = 0. Hence ∫_U a(x)[Dv_e(x)][Dzeta(x)] dx = ∫_U Psi(x)[Dzeta(x)] dx. Together with step 2 this proves the claim. QED

subproblems.title: Local C^{j,alpha} classes are closed under h - (finite sum) and under modification outside U
subproblems.statement: Let n, j, N be natural numbers, alpha real, E a real normed space, U an open subset of R^n, and h, g : R^n -> E and f_1, ..., f_N : R^n -> E (indexed by Fin N). Assume h and every f_i are C^j on U and their j-th derivatives (iteratedFDeriv R j) are alpha-Hoelder on every compact subset of U, and g(x) = h(x) - Σ_i f_i(x) for every x in U. Then g is C^j on U and its j-th derivative is alpha-Hoelder on every compact subset of U.
subproblems.lean_statement: ∀ (n : ℕ) (E : Type) [NormedAddCommGroup E] [NormedSpace ℝ E] (j N : ℕ) (α : ℝ) (U : Set (Rn n)) (h g : Rn n → E) (f : Fin N → Rn n → E), IsOpen U → ContDiffOn ℝ j h U → (∀ K : Set (Rn n), IsCompact K → K ⊆ U → ∃ C : ℝ, ∀ x ∈ K, ∀ y ∈ K, ‖iteratedFDeriv ℝ j h x - iteratedFDeriv ℝ j h y‖ ≤ C * ‖x - y‖ ^ α) → (∀ i : Fin N, ContDiffOn ℝ j (f i) U ∧ ∀ K : Set (Rn n), IsCompact K → K ⊆ U → ∃ C : ℝ, ∀ x ∈ K, ∀ y ∈ K, ‖iteratedFDeriv ℝ j (f i) x - iteratedFDeriv ℝ j (f i) y‖ ≤ C * ‖x - y‖ ^ α) → (∀ x ∈ U, g x = h x - ∑ i, f i x) → ContDiffOn ℝ j g U ∧ ∀ K : Set (Rn n), IsCompact K → K ⊆ U → ∃ C : ℝ, ∀ x ∈ K, ∀ y ∈ K, ‖iteratedFDeriv ℝ j g x - iteratedFDeriv ℝ j g y‖ ≤ C * ‖x - y‖ ^ α
subproblems.natural_proof:
Source: the closure step 'finite sums and differences preserve C^{m-1,alpha}_loc (D^{m-1} is linear on U)' in step 9(iii) of the parent proof, together with the transfer from the pointwise formula on U.
1. Let G := h - Σ_i f_i as a function on R^n. G is C^j on U (ContDiffOn.sub, ContDiffOn.sum over Finset.univ), and g = G on U, so g is C^j on U (ContDiffOn.congr).
2. Pointwise identity of derivatives. Let x in U. Since U is open, g and G agree on the neighbourhood U of x, i.e. g =ᶠ[𝓝 x] G, hence iteratedFDeriv R j g x = iteratedFDeriv R j G x (Filter.EventuallyEq.iteratedFDeriv). Moreover h and all f_i are C^j at x (ContDiffOn.contDiffAt with U ∈ 𝓝 x), and so is Σ_i f_i; hence iteratedFDeriv R j G x = iteratedFDeriv R j h x - Σ_i iteratedFDeriv R j f_i x (iteratedFDeriv_sub_apply and iteratedFDeriv_sum_apply, both requiring only ContDiffAt at x).
3. Fix a compact K ⊆ U. The hypotheses give constants C_h and C_i (i in Fin N) with ||D^j h(x) - D^j h(y)|| ≤ C_h |x - y|^alpha and ||D^j f_i(x) - D^j f_i(y)|| ≤ C_i |x - y|^alpha for x, y in K. Replacing them by max(C_h, 0) and max(C_i, 0) keeps the bounds valid because |x - y|^alpha ≥ 0.
4. For x, y in K ⊆ U, step 2 and the triangle inequality (norm_sub_le, norm_sum_le) give
   ||D^j g(x) - D^j g(y)|| = ||(D^j h(x) - D^j h(y)) - Σ_i (D^j f_i(x) - D^j f_i(y))|| ≤ ||D^j h(x) - D^j h(y)|| + Σ_i ||D^j f_i(x) - D^j f_i(y)|| ≤ (max(C_h, 0) + Σ_i max(C_i, 0)) |x - y|^alpha.
   This is the required bound with C := max(C_h, 0) + Σ_i max(C_i, 0). Together with step 1 the claim follows. QED
